description: Turning raw sequencing reads into biological answers: sequencing technologies and their error profiles, read quality control, mapping to a reference, de novo genome assembly, variant calling and annotation, RNA-seq gene expression analysis, and pathogen genomics for outbreak surveillance. Practised as complete analysis pipelines run on small public datasets with browser-based tools, working through cases such as Vibrio cholerae and Lassa virus genomes and human variants shaped by malaria.
modelledOn: Compeau and Pevzner, Bioinformatics Algorithms: An Active Learning Approach
WHO, Global Genomic Surveillance Strategy for Pathogens with Pandemic and Epidemic Potential
outcomes: Compare short-read and long-read sequencing technologies and choose a platform, read length and depth suited to a genomic question.
Assess and clean raw reads using quality scores, adapter trimming and duplication metrics, and justify each filtering decision.
Map reads to a reference genome with indexed aligners and interpret SAM and BAM records, mapping quality and coverage.
Assemble a genome from reads with de Bruijn and overlap graph methods and evaluate the assembly with contiguity and completeness measures.
Call, filter and annotate genetic variants and analyse differential gene expression from RNA-seq counts with appropriate statistics.
Apply pathogen genomics to outbreak surveillance, from sample to lineage assignment and resistance prediction, and report the findings to public health teams.

units.title: Genomes and sequencing technologies
topics: Genome organisation in bacteria, viruses and eukaryotes: genes, repeats, plasmids, ploidy; the human reference genome
Sanger sequencing and the move to massively parallel sequencing; cost and throughput
Illumina sequencing by synthesis: library preparation, cluster amplification, single-end and paired-end reads
Long-read technologies: nanopore sequencing (MinION) and PacBio HiFi; error profiles and when long reads are essential
Experimental design: coverage and depth (Lander-Waterman), multiplexing and barcodes, whole-genome versus exome versus amplicon
Portable sequencing for field surveillance: nanopore runs in national and regional laboratories in Africa

units.title: Read quality control
topics: FASTQ in depth: Phred scores, encodings, per-base and per-read quality
Quality reports with FastQC and MultiQC: base composition, GC distribution, overrepresented sequences, duplication
Adapter and quality trimming; length filtering; removing host and contaminant reads
Quality control for nanopore reads: read length distributions and basecalling accuracy
Recording QC decisions so an analysis can be reproduced

units.title: Read mapping
topics: Why mapping differs from classical alignment: speed, seeds and the scale of the problem
Indexing a reference: suffix arrays, the Burrows-Wheeler transform and the FM-index; backward search
Short-read aligners (BWA, Bowtie2) and long-read aligners (minimap2); paired-end constraints
SAM and BAM formats: flags, CIGAR strings, mapping quality; sorting, indexing and viewing with samtools
Coverage, insert size and duplicate marking; inspecting alignments in a genome browser

units.title: Genome assembly
topics: The assembly problem: reads, overlaps, contigs and scaffolds; why repeats make it hard
Overlap-layout-consensus and string graphs for long reads
De Bruijn graphs from k-mers: Eulerian paths, choice of k, error correction, bubbles and tips
Assemblers in practice: SPAdes for bacteria, Flye for long reads; hybrid assembly
Evaluating assemblies: N50, misassemblies, BUSCO completeness, comparison with a reference
Genome annotation basics: gene prediction and functional labelling of a bacterial assembly

units.title: Variant calling
topics: Types of variation: SNVs, indels, structural variants, copy-number variation
Genotype likelihoods and Bayesian variant calling; how base and mapping quality enter the model
Calling pipelines: GATK best practices and bcftools; base quality recalibration and joint genotyping
The VCF format; hard filtering versus model-based filtering; transition/transversion ratio as a sanity check
Variant annotation and effect prediction; population databases such as gnomAD and the under-representation of African genomes
Case study: the HbS allele, G6PD deficiency and other human variants shaped by malaria selection

units.title: Gene expression analysis
topics: RNA-seq experimental design: replicates, depth, batch effects, stranded and poly-A libraries
Spliced alignment and pseudo-alignment for quantification (HISAT2, Salmon); counts per gene
Normalisation: library size, TPM, size factors; exploratory analysis with PCA and clustering
Differential expression with negative binomial models (DESeq2, edgeR); multiple testing and the false discovery rate
Interpreting results: volcano plots, gene set and pathway enrichment
Single-cell RNA-seq in brief

units.title: Pathogen genomics for disease surveillance
topics: From sample to sequence in an outbreak: amplicon schemes, turnaround time and laboratory networks
Lineage and genotype assignment for SARS-CoV-2, Vibrio cholerae and Lassa virus; typing schemes such as MLST
Antimicrobial resistance prediction from genomes; resistance gene databases
Linking genomes to case data; sharing sequences through public archives and GISAID
Case study: genomic surveillance of cholera and Lassa fever in West Africa and the Africa CDC Pathogen Genomics Initiative

units.title: Reproducible pipelines and project
topics: Workflow managers (Snakemake, Nextflow) and containers for reproducible pipelines
Compute, storage and cost on limited infrastructure; working with shared servers and the cloud
Ethics and governance of genomic data: consent, community engagement, benefit sharing, data sovereignty in Africa
Project: an end-to-end analysis of a public bacterial or viral outbreak dataset with a surveillance report

schedule.title: Genomes and sequencing technologies
schedule.exercise: Compare Sanger and Illumina sequencing in a half-page table covering read length, accuracy, cost per base and best uses.

tasks.title: Compute genome size, gene count and repeat fraction from a small annotation table for a bacterium, a virus and a plasmid using a short script
Plot the cost per megabase of sequencing from given yearly values and fit a trend to estimate when a 30x human genome fell below a target price
Simulate cluster generation and paired-end reads from a 5 kb reference and check that the insert size distribution matches the library design

schedule.title: Long reads and experimental design
schedule.exercise: Plan the sequencing run for a bacterial outbreak of 24 isolates, stating platform, barcodes and expected depth per isolate.

tasks.title: Simulate reads with a 1 percent and a 10 percent error rate from a 2 kb sequence and compare how many exact k-mer matches each keeps
Compute expected coverage and the fraction of genome uncovered from Lander-Waterman for five read depths and find the minimum depth for 99 percent
Plan a nanopore surveillance run in a regional lab with limited power and cold chain, choosing kit, samples and fallback in the scenario

schedule.title: FASTQ and quality control
schedule.exercise: Interpret a FastQC style report excerpt and write three sentences stating what is wrong with the library and what to do about it.

tasks.title: Decode Phred quality characters in 10 FASTQ records and compute the error probability and mean quality for each read
Write a trimmer that removes adapters and low-quality tails and report how many reads survive in a 1000-read file
Produce per-base quality, GC content and duplication summaries for a FASTQ file, flag the failed checks and compare two runs

schedule.title: Read mapping and indexing
schedule.exercise: Explain with a small worked example why backward search on the FM-index finds a read in time proportional to its length.

tasks.title: Step through the Burrows-Wheeler transform of a short string and perform a backward search for a 3-letter pattern, recording the interval at each step
Build a suffix array and FM-index for a 200 bp reference, then use them to locate 20 short reads with a script
Write a seed-and-extend mapper that tolerates up to two mismatches and test it on 100 simulated paired-end reads, reporting the mapped fraction

schedule.title: Alignment files and coverage
schedule.exercise: Read a few SAM lines by hand and explain every field, including the flag and the CIGAR string.

tasks.title: Decode the flag and CIGAR strings of 10 SAM records and state for each read whether it is paired, mapped and reverse complemented
Compute per-base coverage and mean insert size from a small alignment, mark duplicates and plot the coverage along the reference
Load alignment records into tables and write queries that find regions with coverage below 10x and pairs with abnormal insert sizes

schedule.title: Genome assembly theory
schedule.exercise: Explain why repeats longer than the read length cannot be resolved and what kind of data would resolve them.

tasks.title: Assemble 12 short overlapping reads into contigs by greedy overlap merging and state where a repeat causes ambiguity
Build a de Bruijn graph from the reads of a 30 base sequence at k equals 4, then trace an Eulerian path to reconstruct it
Assemble reads with errors using a de Bruijn graph, pick k to minimise tips and bubbles, and report the contig length and errors left

schedule.title: Assemblers, evaluation and annotation
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page comparison of assembling a bacterial genome with short reads, long reads and a hybrid approach.

tasks.title: Compute N50 and total length from a list of contig sizes and say whether the assembly meets a target of N50 above 100 kb
Find open reading frames of at least 300 bases in a bacterial contig on both strands and label the longest five with start and stop codons
Compare two assemblies of the same genome by N50, misassembly count and completeness against a reference, then recommend one for surveillance

schedule.title: Variant calling
schedule.exercise: Compute by hand the probability that a SNV is real from base quality and coverage in a tiny example and say what threshold you would use.

tasks.title: Classify 10 given differences between a sample and a reference as SNVs, indels or structural variants and write their positions
Implement a simple Bayesian genotype caller for a haploid site using base qualities and test it on 20 pileup columns
Run a simplified calling pipeline on simulated reads with 50 planted variants and report sensitivity and false discoveries

schedule.title: Variant files, annotation and human variation
schedule.exercise: Explain why population databases that mostly contain non-African genomes can mislead variant interpretation for patients in Ghana.

tasks.title: Parse a small VCF, apply hard filters on depth and quality, and compute the transition to transversion ratio as a sanity check
Load variants and an annotation table into a database and write a query that lists the protein-changing variants rarer than 1 percent
Compute allele frequencies of the HbS allele across five West African populations from given counts and test the link with malaria prevalence

schedule.title: RNA-seq design, quantification and normalisation
schedule.exercise: Design an RNA-seq experiment with enough replicates to compare treated and untreated samples and explain your choices.

tasks.title: Check a small RNA-seq sample table for batch effects by plotting condition against sequencing batch and state if the design is confounded
Count reads per gene from given alignments, compute TPM for 10 genes and compare with raw counts
Normalise a counts matrix by size factors, run a PCA on the samples and say whether replicates cluster as expected

schedule.title: Differential expression and single-cell
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why testing 20000 genes needs a false discovery rate correction.

tasks.title: Test 10 genes for differential expression between groups with a simple model and compute adjusted p-values by the Benjamini-Hochberg method
Draw a volcano plot of a results table and run an enrichment test of a pathway among the top genes to report which pathways are significant
Join differential expression results to a gene set table with queries and find pathways enriched among up-regulated genes while controlling the false discovery rate

schedule.title: Genomic surveillance of outbreaks
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page surveillance bulletin for a regional health office summarising what the genomic data say about a cholera outbreak.

tasks.title: Plan the sample-to-sequence workflow for an outbreak with a 72-hour turnaround target and decide which steps to shorten in the scenario
Search assembled genomes for resistance gene sequences from a small database and report the predicted resistance profile for 10 isolates
Link sequence lineages to case data in tables and write queries that show clusters by district and week, flagging a possible transmission chain

schedule.title: Reproducible pipelines, governance and project
schedule.exercise: Write a data sharing and consent statement for a genomic study in a Ghanaian community, covering ownership and benefit sharing.

tasks.title: Write a small workflow script with named steps and dependencies that reruns only the changed step when an input file is modified
Handle a request to share outbreak genomes with a foreign partner by weighing consent, community interests and data sovereignty in the scenario
Run an end-to-end analysis on a public bacterial outbreak dataset, from quality control to lineage and resistance, and write a one-page surveillance report
